meta.title: Student Movies

locator_titles.nausicaa-of-the-valley-of-the-wind: Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind

meta.caveat: Deliberately conservative. These are films with a worksheet, not instruction, so nothing is rated strong. 'Partial' means a worksheet question asks students to think about the competency; 'related' means the film shows it but no question asks about it. Mapped from each worksheet's reflection questions (Part 2) and the CASEL labels in each film's teacher notes; the students' answers were not checked. Only CASEL is mapped, plus one AP CSP code for Ron's Gone Wrong. Computer science films (Wild Robot, WALL-E, Big Hero 6, Spare Parts) have light entries because their worksheets ask about computing, not social-emotional skills.

alignment_log.scope: First pass: all 15 films against casel, plus apcsp 5.6 for Ron's Gone Wrong
alignment_log.note: Read each worksheet's Part 2 questions and matched them to this repo's CASEL catalog. No strong entries on purpose. Left out: CDE T-SEL, Common Core speaking and writing (the worksheets are writing prompts, but writing is not what the films are for), and the CS frameworks other than the one code above.

SA.1.note: Reflection questions and story moments in these films connect to this competency; none of the films teaches it as an activity.

locator_notes.wreck-it-ralph: A worksheet question asks how labels from other people (Ralph is 'the bad guy') shape how we see ourselves.
locator_notes.turning-red: A worksheet question asks why people act differently at home and with friends, and which Mei seems most real.
locator_notes.inside-out-2: Riley's Sense of Self is rebuilt by Anxiety; the worksheet asks about accepting all parts of yourself, but not about identity directly.
